newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates normalise after month-end.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates normalise after month-end.

text.p: German call money rates on Monday traded around 3.10 percent, having come off Friday's high month-end levels, and dealers predicted that rates could come off further in coming sessions.
The bulk of trades was conducted at 3.10 percent today with rates moving between 3.08/12 percent, down from Friday's rates of 4.00/25 percent, dealers said.

Money market conditions had largely normalised after Friday's month-end scramble to meet reserve requirements, they added. But they expected rates would come off further, heading towards the 3.05/10 percent level in the next few days.
Dealers said reserve holdings at the Bundesbank were fairly ample which hinted that money market rates could come off further in the next few days.
Generally dealers expected the Bundesbnak is still interested in keeping rates around the three percent level where it has kept its main money market rate, the repo, since late August.

The Bundesbank said banks held 43.6 billion marks in reserve on Friday, down from 44.3 billion marks held on Thursday. The monthly average rate was at 41.5 billion marks, compared with 41.4 billion marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was set at 3.12383 percent on Monday after being set at 4.21667 percent on Friday.
